subject: Sharing variance parameters across multiple parameters

messages.author: 0e8054b18ece3e51
messages.subject: Sharing variance parameters across multiple parameters
parts:
Dear all,

I have a specific question that I cannot seem to answer myself. In short, I want multiple series, with different indexing, to share a variance parameter. I am aware that when the variables follow the same index, you can use the replicate command. However, I don't know what to do if they have different indexes altogether. Also, the copy trick doesn't work in this case. (I think...)

For example, take;
# library(INLA)
n      = 100
index1 = rep(1:3, n)
index2 = rep(1:3, each=n)

# Note that;
> head(index1)
[1] 1 2 3 1 2 3
> head(index2)
[1] 1 1 1 1 1 1

y      = rnorm(n, 0, 1)
myData = cbind.data.frame(y,index1,index2)

# what I would like is something along the lines of;
inla.formula = y ~ f(index1, model = "rw2") + f(index2, model = "rw2")
inla.model   = inla(formula, family = "gaussian", data = myData)

My question in this case is can ensure that f(index1, model = "rw2") and f(index2, model = "rw2") share the same variance parameter? Also, in this case the maximum of both variables is 3, but this could be different in my application.
In my model I want to group a few of the variance parameters to reduce the amount of hyper parameters to estimate. (I also have a reason why I think they should be similar.) My hope is, it will reduce computational time. 

As always, many thanks and kind regards,
Alex

Here is an example. you can define a model, like rw2, on locations
that you do not use. replicated models share the hyperparameter(s).

H

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Sharing variance parameters across multiple parameters
parts:
Thank you so much for your quick response, this is helpful. 

I do have a follow up question. I actually have used a sort of similar trick before when modelling jointly longitudinal and survival models. In that case there are two different ``y variables'' (one continuous, and one a ``count'' variable).

Going through your code, it seems like a similar ``trick'', i.e. have two y variables and subsequently make one long y vector of length 2 x N. My example is slightly different, because I only have 1 (vector) y variable, size 1 x N. To be more specific, my y variable is the price firms are willing to pay for real estate. On the right hand side I have many continuous variables, like firm debt, enterprise value, etc. I ``bucket'' the right hand-side variables into many quantiles, and subsequently want to look the effects in the extremes. I want to structure these parameters for obvious (signal extraction) reasons; This is why I need the f(x, model="rw2"). My problem is that I have many variables, and thus many variance parameters. Therefore I want to let them share one hyperparamter, hopefully reducing computational time, as I have 15K observations.

If I understand your example correctly, I would have to duplicate the y variable for every x variable that I use? This would blow up the data going into INLA to over 100K. So I am afraid this would actually hurt computational time... 

Any thoughts? Many thanks again,
Alex

Hi,

allthough what you say can be done in some way, are you sure it is a
good approach? If you want to look at the effects in the extremes, do
you then plan to use one of the 'extreme' likelihoods? If than case,
I guess you can go simpler on the exploratory variables.

H
